title: Why a pipeline stalls: the three hazards

items.stem: A processor has one divider unit that cannot start a new division until the last one finishes. Two divide instructions come back to back, and the second has to wait. Which kind of hazard is this?

options.text: A data hazard, because both divide numbers
A structural hazard, because one unit is shared
A control hazard, because the second one waits

items.stem: A pipeline fetches the two instructions after a conditional branch, then finds out the branch is taken and throws them away. Which kind of hazard caused the wasted cycles?

options.text: A data hazard, because the branch reads registers
A structural hazard, because fetch and branch collide
A control hazard, because the next address was unknown

items.stem: A 5-stage pipeline would finish 6 instructions in the ideal number of cycles with no hazards. In this program, hazards cost 3 stall cycles in total. How many cycles does the program take?
In a program, 25% of the instructions are branches, and each branch costs 2 stall cycles. There are no other stalls. What is the average number of cycles per instruction (CPI)?
A student says: "A pipeline stalls only when an instruction needs a result that an earlier instruction has not produced yet." In one sentence, say what is wrong with this.
